chunks: We were told by my father, and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid, may Allah grant them both mercy, that they both said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah told us, that he said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa told us, from al-Hasan ibn Ali and al-Washsha', from Ahmad ibn A'idh, from Abu Khadija, Salem ibn Makram the Cameleer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding the saying of Him, Exalted and Glorious is He: 'except for the weakened ones from the men, women and children; they cannot devise a plan, nor are they guided to a path', so he said: They are unable to devise a plan towards Nusb [antagonism] by which they antagonize, nor are they guided to the path of the people of the truth by which they enter into it. These people will enter Paradise for good deeds and by refraining from the forbidden things which Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He, has prohibited, and they will not attain the ranks of the righteous.

key_terms.النُّصْب: Antagonism or striving (specifically in the context of jihad or religious duty)
key_terms.الْأَبْرَار: The righteous (those of high spiritual rank)
key_terms.الْمُسْتَضْعَفِينَ: The weakened (those unable to perform duties due to weakness or captivity)

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'the weakened' in Quran 4:98 according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq elucidates that the 'weakened' are exempt from full obligations because they lack the capacity for 'Nusb' (active striving or exertion) and cannot discern the path of truth, leading to a nuanced eschatological status. While they enter Paradise through good deeds and avoiding prohibitions, they do not attain the elevated ranks of the 'Abrar' (the supremely righteous), highlighting a distinction between general salvation and spiritual excellence in Shia exegesis. This interpretation underscores the balance between divine mercy for the incapable and the merit of active adherence to the Ahl al-Bayt's guidance.
